top_signals.title: US Stocks Drop, Led by Tech, as Bond-Yield Spike Sparks Angst
top_signals.summary: US stocks fell at the open on Tuesday as rising bond yields and an early-morning spike in oil prices unnerved investors, prompting them to pare back some of their riskier trades including bets on AI and related tech.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Commodity repricing impacting inflation expectations and industrial supply chains.

top_signals.title: Chip Stocks Get Hit as Global Bond Anxiety Builds: Markets Wrap
top_signals.summary: Wall Street was rattled by a selloff in chipmakers, with stocks also falling as concerns about inflation and rising government debt lifted bond yields.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Inflation expectations impacting rate path, bonds and global risk assets.

top_signals.title: Global Bonds Slump Sends Borrowing Costs Soaring
top_signals.summary: Long-term borrowing costs have hit their highest level in decades on the back of a global bond slump. Alex Morgan explains. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.
